Definition: a body, whether alive or dead
BiblicalUsage: gᵉvîyâh means a body (of living creatures). It occurs 11 times in all, and the passages I have picked — Genesis, Judges, 1 Samuel, and Nehemiah — show it in its plain sense. I read it as a word that does its work quietly, without dressing anything up.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe gᵉvîyâh matters because the body matters to God; He made it, and He will raise it. I hold that reading it plainly keeps me honest about what God actually said.
RelatedEvents: Saul's Death at Gilboa; Israel Renews the Covenant
